critical_operation.code_excerpt:
defp handle_in(nil, %{event: "phx_join", topic: topic, ref: ref, join_ref: join_ref} = message, state, socket) do
    case socket.handler.__channel__(topic) do
      {channel, opts} ->
        case Phoenix.Channel.Server.join(socket, channel, message, opts) do
          {:ok, reply, pid} ->
            reply = %Reply{join_ref: join_ref, ref: ref, topic: topic, status: :ok, payload: reply}
            state = put_channel(state, pid, topic, join_ref)
critical_operation.description: Each transport process (WebSocket or LongPoll) runs Phoenix.Socket.handle_in/4. The phx_join clause (595-613) resolves socket.handler.__channel__(topic) and, when a channel module is returned, calls Phoenix.Channel.Server.join/4 (line 598) and records the returned pid in state.channels via put_channel/4; the state created in user_connect/6 (line 544) contains only channels and channels_inverse, with no count, no per-transport ceiling and no rate limit. A client can therefore send phx_join messages for many acceptable topics over one connection and each accepted join leaves a persistent channel process, so a single unauthenticated transport can allocate processes without bound and exhaust the node. Persistence requires the resolved channel's join/3 to accept the topic (a wildcard channel such as room:* qualifies); joins the channel rejects do not leave a persistent process. The 1.6.17 fix adds max_channels_per_transport (default 100) to the transport state and rejects further joins with status :error once map_size(state.channels) reaches the limit (CWE-770).

entry_point.description: A remote client connects to a mounted Phoenix socket transport and sends repeated phx_join messages on the same WebSocket or LongPoll connection.

trace.description: the transport state is initialized without any channel-count limit
handle_in/4 receives each phx_join from the transport
every join starts a channel process and its pid is stored
the pid is added to state.channels with no cap

verification_method: Static read of lib/phoenix/socket.ex at v1.6.13 and v1.6.17, the 1.6 fix commit and its tests, plus git ancestry; no Phoenix node or WebSocket client was executed.
